messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide to generate a **GET** request for the “Device Connector Versions” API on Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1. The instructions assume you already have an account and the necessary permissions to view the API documentation. --- ## 1. Log In & Open the API Explorer | Step | What to do | Screenshot? | |------|------------|--------------| | 1 | Open your browser and navigate to the Nexus Dashboard URL (e.g. `https://nexus-dashboard.example.com`). | – | | 2 | Log in with your credentials. | – | | 3 | From the left‑hand menu, click **Developer** → **API Explorer** (or **API Docs**). | – | > **Tip:** If you don’t see the API Explorer, you may need to enable the *Developer* role in your user profile. --- ## 2. Locate the Endpoint 1. In the API Explorer, expand the **Device Connector** section. 2. Find the operation named **Get information of device connector versions** (or similar). 3. Click the operation to open its details. You should now see: - **HTTP Method:** `GET` - **Endpoint URL:** `/api/v1/device-connector/versions` (the exact path may vary; copy the full URL shown) - **Parameters:** none (unless you see optional query parameters) - **Headers:** `Authorization: Bearer ` (required) --- ## 3. Generate the Request ### 3.1 Using the Built‑in “Generate cURL” Button 1. In the operation details pane, click **Generate cURL**. 2. A pre‑filled cURL command will appear, e.g.: ```bash curl -X GET "https://nexus-dashboard.example.com/api/v1/device-connector/versions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` Copy this command and run it in your terminal. ### 3.2 Using Postman 1. Click **Generate Postman Collection** (if available). 2. Import the collection into Postman. 3. Open the request, replace `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN` with a valid token, and hit **Send**. ### 3.3 Using Python (via the provided `requests_get` function) If you prefer to call the API programmatically, you can use the `requests_get` helper. Below is a sample call (replace the URL and token accordingly): ```python from functions import requests_get url = "https://nexus-dashboard.example.com/api/v1/device-connector/versions" headers = { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN", "Accept": "application/json" } response = requests_get(url=url, params={}, headers=headers) print(response.json()) ``` > **Note:** The `requests_get` function in the tool namespace expects only `url` and `params`. > If you need to pass custom headers, you’ll have to modify the function or use a standard `requests.get()` call. --- ## 4. Inspect the Response A successful call returns a JSON payload similar to: ```json { "deviceConnectorVersions": [ { "name": "ConnectorA", "version": "1.2.3", "releaseDate": "2024-01-15" }, { "name": "ConnectorB", "version": "4.5.6", "releaseDate": "2024-02-20" } ], "totalCount": 2 } ``` If you receive a **401 Unauthorized**, double‑check that: - The token is still valid (refresh if needed). - The token has the `api.read` scope (or equivalent). If you receive a **404 Not Found**, verify that the endpoint path matches the one shown in the API Explorer. --- ## 5. Automate the Call (Optional) If you want to schedule regular checks: 1. Store the access token in a secure vault (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager). 2. Use a cron job or a CI/CD pipeline to run the script above. 3. Parse the JSON and trigger alerts if a new version appears. --- ### Quick Reference | Item | Value | |------|-------| | **Method** | GET | | **Endpoint** | `/api/v1/device-connector/versions` | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | | **Query Params** | None (unless documented) | | **Sample cURL** | `curl -X GET "https://nexus-dashboard.example.com/api/v1/device-connector/versions" -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/json"` | --- #### Need Help? - **Token Issues:** Contact your Nexus Dashboard admin to obtain a new token. - **Endpoint Changes:** Check the “Changelog” tab in the API Explorer for any recent updates. - **Rate Limits:** The API may enforce a limit of X requests per minute; consult the docs for details. Happy querying!
